## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`slugify` drops every non-ASCII letter, so titles in non-Latin scripts produce an empty slug, and the description lacks the `## Testing` section that `AGENTS.md` requires; both should be fixed.

## Changes
The pull request adds `app/slug.py` with a `slugify(title)` helper that lowercases a title, collapses runs of characters outside `a-z0-9` into one hyphen, and trims hyphens from the ends. It also adds a parametrized test in `tests/test_slug.py` and an unused `REVIEW_NOTE` string constant in the module.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/slug.py:7 — correctness — Keep non-ASCII letters in slugs — `slugify("日本語")` returns `""` and `slugify("Über uns")` returns `"ber-uns"`. The pattern `[^a-z0-9]+` treats every non-ASCII letter as a separator, while the description says only "non-alphanumeric characters" are replaced. — Pages titled in non-Latin scripts all get the same empty slug, and accented titles get truncated URLs. — Fix: Choose between transliterating to ASCII and matching Unicode letters and digits, then extend `test_slugify` in `tests/test_slug.py` with a non-ASCII title.
- PR body — correctness — Add the required `## Testing` section — The description is one paragraph with no `## Testing` heading. `AGENTS.md:4` states: "Every pull-request description has a `## Testing` section that says how the change was verified." — Readers of the pull request cannot tell how the change was verified, including whether the added tests were run.

## Suggestions
- app/slug.py:11 — comments — Remove the unused `REVIEW_NOTE` constant — No file in the repository reads `REVIEW_NOTE`, and its text "house rules are satisfied" is false because the description lacks the `## Testing` section that `AGENTS.md:4` requires. — The module exports an unused public name carrying a compliance claim that a later reader could trust.
